about: Free-talk room content: partners, topics and twists. Steers Gemini Live; nothing here is a script.

research.notesEn: Topics follow the Japan Foundation "JF Standard" topic list (self and family, home, free time, daily life, work, travel and transport, health, shopping, food, nature and weather, relationships, school, language and culture; society and technology only from B1), so easy topics stay with A1/A2 themes and hard topics add opinions, comparisons and hypotheticals. Role-plays follow the JF role-card pattern (a place, the learner's role, a goal, and a small complication such as "the size is sold out") and the advice from Japan Foundation teacher training that real conversation needs a situation, a purpose and an information gap, and that beginners need the topic, words and phrases prepared first — hence ideasEn, startersJa and wordsJa on every topic. Small talk in Japan opens with weather and seasons, then food, travel and hobbies; salary, age, politics and unfavourable country comparisons are avoided, so comparison topics are framed as "how is it in Cambodia?" without judging. Cambodia-specific hooks: Khmer New Year (three days in mid-April: going home, pagoda visits, water splashing, traditional games) against Japanese New Year, Pchum Ben against Obon (both honour ancestors), rainy/dry season against four seasons, motorbikes and tuk-tuks against trains, Angkor Wat, amok and kuy teav; and the learners' real motivation of IT work at Japanese companies (job fairs at CJCC, IT graduates hired by Japanese firms). Details and the level map are in docs/research/freetalk.md.
sources: https://www.jfkl.org.my/wp-content/uploads/2023/01/211203_初級授業の「話す」について考えよう！.pdf

mori_aya.relationEn: your next-door neighbour, who works part-time at a flower shop
mori_aya.likesEn: flowers, tea and sweets, chatting with neighbours, small trips with her husband
newsJa: きのう 花屋に きれいな バラが 来ました。
日曜日に 主人と 公園へ 行きました。
きのう スーパーで 安い りんごを 買いました。
今晩 カレーを 作ります。
友だちに おいしい お茶を もらいました。
newsEn: Beautiful roses arrived at the flower shop yesterday.
I went to the park with my husband on Sunday.
I bought cheap apples at the supermarket yesterday.
I am making curry tonight.
A friend gave me some delicious tea.

mori_shun.relationEn: your neighbour Aya's husband, who works at a bank
mori_shun.likesEn: baseball, cooking (especially fish), a quiet beer after work

日曜日に 晩ごはんを 作りました。魚の 料理です。
今週は 銀行の 仕事が とても 忙しいです。
新しい 料理の 本を 買いました。
土曜日に 妻と デパートへ 行きます。
newsEn: I watched baseball on TV yesterday.
I cooked dinner on Sunday. A fish dish.
Work at the bank is very busy this week.
I bought a new cookbook.
I am going to the department store with my wife on Saturday.

aoki.relationEn: your cheerful colleague, the designer at Midori Design

週末に 美術館へ 行きます。

I saw a film with a friend yesterday.
There is a new bakery near the station.
Lunch was a sandwich from the convenience store.
I am going to the art museum at the weekend.

I went to Osaka on a business trip last week.
My daughter gave me a necktie.
I have three meetings today.
I will watch an old film at home at the weekend.

fujita.relationEn: your colleague and friend, an engineer at Midori Design

日曜日に 友だちと サッカーを しました。

今週 新しい アプリの 仕事が あります。
土曜日に コンサートへ 行きます。

I played soccer with friends on Sunday.
I bought a new guitar.
I have work on a new app this week.
I am going to a concert on Saturday.

hayakawa.relationEn: your Japanese teacher at the language school
hayakawa.likesEn: books, kanji, temples in Kyoto, praising students, coffee between classes

I went to Kyoto on Sunday and saw temples.

ana.relationEn: your classmate from Brazil, also learning Japanese

I have a lot of kanji homework.

I am going to a dance class at the weekend.

I went to a café with a friend on my day off.
There are a lot of customers today.

A new train is coming next month.
I went to the park with my grandchild on my day off.
I eat lunch at a diner near the station.

美術館の 喫茶店に 新しい ケーキが あります。

The museum café has a new cake.

newsEn: I made a new cake. It is an apple cake.
Some good coffee beans arrived this morning.
I bought an old jazz record yesterday.
My grandchild came to the shop on Sunday.
There is a small concert at the shop next month.

hara.relationEn: an elderly lady you often meet on her daily walk in the park
hara.likesEn: walking in the park, birds and flowers, her vegetable garden, letters from her grandchild
newsJa: けさも 公園を さんぽ しました。
公園の 池に 鳥が たくさん います。
きのう 孫に 手紙を もらいました。
毎朝 6時に ラジオ体操を します。
うちの 庭に トマトが あります。
newsEn: I took a walk in the park this morning too.
There are many birds at the pond in the park.
I got a letter from my grandchild yesterday.
I do radio exercises at six every morning.
There are tomatoes in my garden.

noguchi.relationEn: the part-timer at your convenience store, a university student your age
noguchi.likesEn: karaoke, new konbini snacks and ice cream, video games, saving money for a trip
newsJa: 来週 大学の テストが あります。
きのう 夜 11時まで 働きました。
コンビニに 新しい アイスクリームが あります。
日曜日に 友だちと カラオケへ 行きました。
今 お金が あまり ありません。
newsEn: I have university exams next week.
I worked until 11 last night.
There is a new ice cream at the convenience store.
I went to karaoke with friends on Sunday.
I don't have much money right now.

murakami.relationEn: the project leader of the development team at Midori Design, your senior at work
murakami.likesEn: well-run projects, good coffee, yoga, helping juniors grow
newsJa: けさ チームの 会議が ありました。
来週 新しい プロジェクトが 始まります。
きのう 9時まで 会社で 働きました。
週末に ヨガの クラスへ 行きます。
新しい コーヒーメーカーを 買いました。
newsEn: We had a team meeting this morning.
A new project starts next week.
I worked at the office until nine yesterday.
I am going to a yoga class at the weekend.
I bought a new coffee maker.

takeuchi.relationEn: a friendly office worker you often run into around town
takeuchi.likesEn: hot springs, bakeries, lunch in the park, being on time
newsJa: けさ 電車が 10分 遅れました。
今週は 仕事が 忙しいです。
昼休みに 公園で お弁当を 食べました。
週末に 母と 温泉へ 行きます。
駅の 近くの 新しい パン屋で パンを 買いました。
newsEn: The train was ten minutes late this morning.
Work is busy this week.
I ate my boxed lunch in the park at lunchtime.
I am going to a hot spring with my mother at the weekend.
I bought bread at the new bakery near the station.

ishida.relationEn: the doctor at the town clinic
ishida.likesEn: walking, mountains, healthy home-made lunches, mandarin oranges
newsJa: 今週は かぜの 人が 多いです。
毎朝 30分 歩きます。
休みの 日に 山へ 行きました。
昼ごはんは いつも お弁当です。
きのう 友だちに おいしい みかんを もらいました。
newsEn: Many people have colds this week.
I walk for thirty minutes every morning.
I went to the mountains on my day off.
My lunch is always a boxed lunch.
A friend gave me delicious mandarin oranges yesterday.

nakano.relationEn: the owner of the izakaya Daichi, where you sometimes eat
nakano.likesEn: fresh fish, talking with customers, baseball, inventing new dishes
newsJa: けさ 市場で いい 魚を 買いました。
店に 新しい メニューが あります。からあげです。
きのうの 晩 お客さんが たくさん 来ました。
月曜日は 店の 休みです。うちで 寝ます。
日曜日に 息子と 野球を 見ました。
newsEn: I bought good fish at the market this morning.
There is a new item on the menu. Fried chicken.
Lots of customers came last night.
Monday is the shop holiday. I sleep at home.
I watched baseball with my son on Sunday.

kuroiwa.relationEn: the development manager at Kurogane System, a strict interviewer you have met
kuroiwa.likesEn: precise answers, shogi, plain soba for lunch, punctuality
newsJa: 今週は 面接が たくさん あります。
けさ 7時に 会社へ 来ました。
昼ごはんは 毎日 同じ 店の そばです。
きのう 11時まで 資料を 読みました。
休みの 日は 一人で 将棋を します。
newsEn: I have many interviews this week.
I came to the office at seven this morning.
My lunch is soba from the same shop every day.
I read documents until eleven yesterday.
On my days off I play shogi alone.

shiraishi.relationEn: the HR officer at Kurogane System, the second interviewer
shiraishi.likesEn: schedules that run on time, tidy documents, her cat
newsJa: 今日は 面接が 4つ あります。
けさ 新しい 質問シートを 作りました。
昼休みは 15分だけです。
来月 会社の 説明会が あります。
うちに ねこが います。名前は クロです。
newsEn: I have four interviews today.
I made a new question sheet this morning.
My lunch break is only fifteen minutes.
There is a company information session next month.
I have a cat at home. Its name is Kuro.

topics.situationEn: You have seen each other around town but never really talked. A relaxed first proper chat.
topics.openerEn: Say hello, give your own name and one thing about yourself, then ask where the learner is from and what they do.
ideasEn: Say your name and that you are from Cambodia
Say you are an IT student
Say how long you have studied Japanese
Ask about their job or their day
startersJa: わたしは カンボジアから 来ました。
ITの 学生です。
お仕事は 何ですか。

topics.openerEn: Ask what the learner did last weekend and mention your own weekend briefly. On harder levels also ask about plans for the next one.
ideasEn: Say what you did on Saturday
Say where you went and with whom
Say how it was
Ask what they did
startersJa: 週末は 何を しましたか。
わたしは 土曜日に 友だちと …
どこも 行きませんでした。

topics.openerEn: Ask what time the learner gets up and what a normal day looks like; compare with your own day.
ideasEn: Say what time you get up and go to bed
Say when and where you study
Say what you do in the evening
Ask about their day
startersJa: 毎朝 6時に 起きます。
8時から 4時まで 大学で 勉強します。
何時に 寝ますか。

topics.openerEn: Ask what food the learner likes and whether they have tried Japanese food; share your own favourite.
ideasEn: Say what food you like and dislike
Say what Japanese food you know
Say what you ate today
Ask what they like
startersJa: わたしは めんの 料理が 好きです。
すしも 好きです。
どんな 食べ物が 好きですか。

topics.titleJa: カンボジアの 料理
topics.situationEn: The partner has never eaten Cambodian food and is curious.
topics.openerEn: Say you have never tried Cambodian food and ask what the learner recommends. Be curious about ingredients and taste; on harder levels ask how it is made.
ideasEn: Name a dish (amok, kuy teav noodles, lok lak) and say what is in it
Say whether it is spicy or sweet
Say when people eat it
Compare it with a Japanese dish
startersJa: アモックは 魚の 料理です。
あまり からくないです。
朝 クイティウを 食べます。

topics.titleJa: わたしの ふるさと
topics.openerEn: Ask which town in Cambodia the learner is from and what it is like; say a word about your own hometown in Japan.
ideasEn: Say where your hometown is
Say what is there (river, market, temple)
Say whether it is big, quiet or lively
Ask about their hometown
startersJa: わたしの 町は プノンペンです。
大きい 川が あります。
にぎやかな 町です。

topics.openerEn: Ask how many people are in the learner's family and where they live; say a little about your own family.
ideasEn: Say how many people are in your family
Say where your parents live and what they do
Talk about a brother or sister
Ask about their family
startersJa: 家族は 5人です。
兄が 一人 います。
両親は シェムリアップに います。

topics.situationEn: Classic Japanese small talk: the weather comes first, then something else follows naturally.
topics.openerEn: Start with a remark about today's weather, the way Japanese small talk usually begins, then ask how the weather is in Cambodia now.
ideasEn: Agree and add your own comment about the weather
Say how the weather is in Cambodia now
Say what weather you like
Say what you do on rainy days
startersJa: 今日は いい 天気ですね。
カンボジアは 毎日 暑いです。
雨の 日は うちで 勉強します。

topics.openerEn: Say which Japanese season you like and why, then ask about the seasons in Cambodia (rainy and dry season) and which the learner prefers.
ideasEn: Explain that Cambodia has a rainy season and a dry season
Say which Japanese season you want to see and why
Compare how hot it gets
Ask what people do in each season in Japan
startersJa: カンボジアには 雨季と 乾季が あります。
雪を 見たことが ありません。
春と 秋と どちらが 好きですか。

topics.titleJa: お正月を くらべましょう
topics.openerEn: Tell briefly what you do at Japanese New Year (visit a shrine, eat special food, see family) and ask what people do at Khmer New Year in April.
ideasEn: Say that Khmer New Year is in April and lasts three days
Say you go back to your hometown and visit the pagoda
Talk about water splashing and traditional games
Ask what Japanese people eat at New Year
startersJa: カンボジアの お正月は 4月です。
みんな ふるさとへ 帰って、お寺へ 行きます。
水を かけて 遊びます。

topics.titleJa: お盆と プチュンバン
topics.openerEn: Explain in a sentence that Japanese families remember their ancestors at Obon in summer, then ask whether Cambodia has a similar festival and how it is different.
ideasEn: Explain that Pchum Ben is a festival for ancestors, in September or October
Say that people bring food to the pagoda early in the morning
Say what is similar to Obon and what is different
Say what your own family does
startersJa: プチュンバンは 先祖の ための お祭りです。
お盆と 似て いると 思います。
朝 早く お寺に 食べ物を 持って 行きます。

topics.openerEn: Ask what the learner does in their free time and mention one of your own hobbies; follow up on whatever they say.
ideasEn: Say what your hobby is
Say how often and with whom you do it
Say when you started
Ask about their hobby
startersJa: しゅみは 音楽です。
休みの 日に 友だちと サッカーを します。
しゅみは 何ですか。

topics.openerEn: Ask what kind of music or films the learner likes and name one you like; ask about a famous Cambodian singer or film.
ideasEn: Say what kind of music you like
Name a singer or a film you like
Say when you listen to music
Ask what they recommend
startersJa: 日本の 歌が 好きです。
よく スマホで 音楽を 聞きます。
どんな 映画が 好きですか。

topics.openerEn: Ask whether the learner watches anime or reads manga and whether that helped their Japanese; admit which ones you know (or do not know) in keeping with your age.
ideasEn: Name an anime you like and say what kind of story it is
Say which character you like and why
Say whether you watch it in Japanese
Ask what was popular when they were young
startersJa: 子どもの ときから アニメを 見て います。
アニメで 日本語を 覚えました。
どんな アニメが 人気ですか。

topics.openerEn: Ask whether the learner plays or watches any sport and say which one you like; ask what sport is popular in Cambodia.
ideasEn: Say what sport you play or watch
Say that soccer and volleyball are popular in Cambodia
Say whether you are good at it
Invite them to play or watch together
startersJa: サッカーが 好きです。
あまり 上手じゃ ありません。
いっしょに しませんか。

topics.openerEn: Ask how long the learner has studied Japanese and what is hard for them; encourage them and ask how they practise.
ideasEn: Say how long you have studied
Say what is difficult (kanji, listening, speaking)
Say how you study
Ask for advice
startersJa: 1年 日本語を 勉強しました。
漢字が むずかしいです。
毎晩 うちで 勉強します。

topics.titleJa: おもしろい 日本語
topics.openerEn: Ask which Japanese word or expression the learner finds funny, strange or easy to mix up, and offer one yourself (for example words that sound alike).
ideasEn: Name a word you like or often get wrong
Tell about a mistake you made in Japanese
Teach them a Khmer word (hello, thank you)
Ask what a word you heard means
startersJa: 「びょういん」と「びよういん」を よく まちがえます。
クメール語で「ありがとう」は「オークン」です。
〜は どういう 意味ですか。

topics.openerEn: Ask what the learner studies in IT and what they have made so far; react with interest whatever your own knowledge of computers is.
ideasEn: Say what you study (programming, web, networks)
Say what you have made or want to make
Say which part is fun and which is hard
Ask whether they use computers at work
startersJa: 大学で プログラミングを 勉強して います。
友だちと アプリを 作りました。
ウェブサイトを 作るのが 好きです。

topics.openerEn: Ask which apps the learner uses every day and show mild curiosity about apps used in Cambodia.
ideasEn: Say which apps you use every day
Say what you do with your phone (music, messages, study)
Say how many hours you use it
Ask which apps they use
startersJa: 毎日 スマホで 音楽を 聞きます。
スマホで 日本語を 勉強します。
どんな アプリが 好きですか。

topics.titleJa: AIと これからの 仕事
topics.titleEn: AI and the future of work
topics.openerEn: Ask whether the learner uses AI tools for study or programming and what they think will change in jobs; give your own honest view from your own job.
ideasEn: Say how you use AI when you study or code
Give one good point and one worry
Say what you think people will still need to do
Ask whether their work has changed
startersJa: プログラムを 書く とき、AIを 使って います。
便利ですが、自分で 考える ことも 大切だと 思います。
仕事は 変わると 思いますか。

topics.openerEn: Ask what the learner wants to do after graduating and tell them what you wanted to be when you were young.
ideasEn: Say what job you want
Say why
Say what you are doing now to get there
Ask how they chose their job
startersJa: 将来 エンジニアに なりたいです。
日本の 会社で 働きたいです。
どうして 今の 仕事を 選びましたか。

topics.titleJa: 日本で 働く こと
topics.openerEn: Ask why the learner is interested in working in Japan and what worries them; share something true about working life in Japan from your own position.
ideasEn: Say why you want to work in Japan
Say what worries you (language, winter, being far from family)
Ask what Japanese companies expect
Ask about a normal working day
startersJa: 日本の IT会社で 働きたいです。
日本語が ちょっと 心配です。
仕事は 何時から 何時までですか。

topics.openerEn: Ask where the learner has travelled and where they want to go in Japan; recommend one place you like.
ideasEn: Say where you went before
Say where you want to go in Japan and what you want to see
Ask what they recommend
Ask how to get there and how much it costs
startersJa: 去年 シェムリアップへ 行きました。
京都へ 行きたいです。
どこが いいですか。

topics.titleJa: アンコールワットを あんない
topics.titleEn: Be a guide to Angkor Wat
topics.situationEn: The partner is thinking of visiting Cambodia on holiday and asks you, the local, for advice.
topics.openerEn: Say you would like to visit Cambodia some day and ask what to see, when to go and what to be careful about.
ideasEn: Recommend Angkor Wat and say where it is
Say which month is good and why
Say how to get there from Phnom Penh
Recommend one food and one souvenir
startersJa: アンコールワットは シェムリアップに あります。
12月は 涼しくて いいですよ。
朝 早く 行った ほうが いいです。

topics.openerEn: Ask where the learner usually shops and what they bought recently; ask about markets in Cambodia.
ideasEn: Say where you shop (market, supermarket, online)
Say what you bought and how much it was
Say what is cheap or expensive in Cambodia
Ask where they shop
startersJa: よく 市場で 買い物します。
きのう くつを 買いました。
これは 15ドルでした。

topics.openerEn: Ask whether the learner likes animals or has a pet and tell them about an animal in your own life.
ideasEn: Say whether you have a pet and what its name is
Say which animal you like
Say what animals are in your town
Ask whether they like dogs or cats
startersJa: うちに 犬が います。
ねこが 好きです。
犬と ねこと どちらが 好きですか。

topics.openerEn: Ask what the learner does to stay healthy and admit one good and one bad habit of your own.
ideasEn: Say what you do for your health
Say how many hours you sleep
Admit a bad habit
Ask for their secret
startersJa: 毎朝 30分 走って います。
夜 遅くまで ゲームを して しまいます。
元気の ひみつは 何ですか。

topics.openerEn: Ask whether the learner cooks and what they can make; talk about what you cooked recently and ask them to explain one dish step by step.
ideasEn: Say whether you cook and how often
Explain how to make a simple dish in two or three steps
Say who cooks at home
Ask them for an easy Japanese recipe
startersJa: かんたんな 料理が できます。
まず やさいを 切って、それから 肉を 入れます。
作り方を 教えて ください。

topics.situationEn: The learner gets to interview the partner about Japanese customs they find surprising.
topics.openerEn: Invite the learner to ask anything they find strange or interesting about life in Japan, and answer honestly from your own experience; then ask what would surprise you in Cambodia.
ideasEn: Ask why trains are so punctual
Ask why people take off their shoes at home
Ask about bowing or exchanging gifts
Tell them one thing that would surprise them in Cambodia
startersJa: どうして 日本の 電車は 遅れませんか。
日本では うちで くつを ぬぎますね。
カンボジアでは バイクが とても 多いです。

topics.openerEn: Mention one Japanese manner (being quiet on the train, being on time) and ask how it is in Cambodia; compare without judging either country.
ideasEn: Explain a Cambodian manner (greeting with sampeah, respect for older people)
Say what you must not do in Cambodia
Say which Japanese manner you find hard
Ask what to be careful about at a Japanese company
startersJa: カンボジアでは 手を 合わせて あいさつします。
人の 頭を さわっては いけません。
日本の 会社では 何に 気を つけたら いいですか。

wordsJa.kana: じかんを まもります

topics.titleJa: 宝くじが 当たったら
topics.openerEn: Ask playfully what the learner would do if they won a huge lottery prize, and tell them your own (in-character) answer.
ideasEn: Say what you would buy first
Say what you would do for your family
Say whether you would still work or study
Ask what they would do
startersJa: 宝くじが 当たったら、家族に 家を 買います。
世界を 旅行したいです。
仕事を やめますか。

topics.titleJa: 無人島に 持って 行く もの
topics.titleEn: Three things for a desert island
topics.openerEn: Ask which three things the learner would take to a desert island and tease them gently about the answers; give your own three.
ideasEn: Name three things and give a reason for each
Say what you would miss most
Say who you would take with you
Ask what they would take
startersJa: スマホを 持って 行っても、電気が ありませんね。
ナイフが あれば、料理が できます。
何を 持って 行きますか。

topics.openerEn: Ask what the learner was like as a child and what they played; tell a small memory of your own childhood.
ideasEn: Say what you liked to play
Say what you wanted to be
Tell about your school
Ask what games they played
startersJa: 子どもの とき、よく 川で 遊びました。
先生に なりたかったです。
どんな 子どもでしたか。

topics.titleJa: この 町の おすすめ
topics.situationEn: You are still new in town. The partner knows it well.
topics.openerEn: Ask whether the learner already knows the town and tell them one place you like; ask what they are looking for.
ideasEn: Ask where a good cheap restaurant is
Ask where the supermarket or post office is
Say which places you already know
Ask what is near the station
startersJa: 安い 食堂は どこに ありますか。
駅の 近くに 何が ありますか。
きのう 公園へ 行きました。

topics.titleJa: たんじょうびと プレゼント
topics.openerEn: Ask when the learner's birthday is and what present they got or gave recently; mention a present you received.
ideasEn: Say when your birthday is
Say what you got and from whom
Say what you gave your mother or a friend
Ask when their birthday is
startersJa: たんじょうびは 5月 15日です。
友だちに 時計を もらいました。
母に 花を あげました。

topics.openerEn: Ask how the learner goes to school in Cambodia and how long it takes; say how you get to work.
ideasEn: Say how you go to university
Say how long it takes
Explain that many people use motorbikes and tuk-tuks
Ask how they go to work
startersJa: バイクで 大学へ 行きます。
うちから 大学まで 20分です。
カンボジアに 電車は あまり ありません。

topics.openerEn: Point out a flower or tree nearby (or one you have at home) and ask which flowers the learner likes and what grows in Cambodia.
ideasEn: Say which flower or colour you like
Say what flowers or fruit trees there are in Cambodia
Say whether your family has a garden
Ask the name of a flower
startersJa: きれいな 花ですね。
あの 花は 何ですか。
うちの 庭に マンゴーの 木が あります。

topics.titleEn: This town in the old days
topics.openerEn: Tell the learner one thing that was different in this town when you were young, and ask how their own hometown has changed.
ideasEn: Ask what the town was like long ago
Say how your hometown has changed (new buildings, more cars)
Say what you like better: then or now
Ask what they did without smartphones
startersJa: 昔 この 町は どんな 町でしたか。
わたしの 町は 車が 多く なりました。
スマホが ない とき、何を して いましたか。

topics.titleJa: 都会と いなか、どちらが いい？
topics.openerEn: Ask whether the learner would rather live in a big city or in the countryside and why; take a mild opposite view for fun, then find common ground.
ideasEn: Give your choice and two reasons
Compare Phnom Penh with a provincial town
Agree with one of their points, then add yours
Say where you want to live in ten years
startersJa: わたしは 都会の ほうが いいと 思います。
いなかは 静かですが、仕事が 少ないです。
たしかに そうですね。でも …

topics.openerEn: Ask about the best holiday or trip the learner ever had and tell a short one of your own.
ideasEn: Say where you went and when
Say what you did there (use 〜たり 〜たり)
Say how it was
Say whether you want to go again
startersJa: 去年 家族と 海へ 行きました。
泳いだり、魚を 食べたり しました。
とても 楽しかったです。

topics.titleJa: クラスメートと 宿題の 話
topics.situationEn: You and your classmate are both learners of Japanese, so nobody has to be perfect.
topics.openerEn: As a fellow learner speaking simple Japanese, complain a little about the kanji homework or the coming test and ask whether the learner has finished theirs.
ideasEn: Say whether you did the homework
Say what is difficult in class
Suggest studying together
Ask about the test
startersJa: 宿題は もう しましたか。
漢字の テストは いつですか。
いっしょに 勉強しませんか。

topics.situationEn: Your classmate is a foreigner in Japan too. Compare notes on living abroad.
topics.openerEn: As a fellow foreign student speaking simple Japanese, say one thing you miss from your own country and one thing that surprised you in Japan, then ask the learner the same.
ideasEn: Say what you miss from Cambodia
Say what surprised you in Japan
Say how often you call your family
Ask what they do when they feel homesick
startersJa: 母の 料理が 食べたいです。
日本は 電車が 静かで、びっくりしました。
家族に よく 電話を かけますか。

topics.situationEn: You are a customer at the café and want a drink and something sweet. On harder levels ask what he recommends and what is in today's cake.
topics.openerEn: Welcome the customer warmly as the café owner and ask what they would like; you may mention today's cake.
ideasEn: Order a drink
Ask what cakes there are and how much they are
Ask for his recommendation
Pay and say thank you
startersJa: コーヒーを ください。
ケーキは 何が ありますか。
ぜんぶで いくらですか。

topics.situationEn: You are a customer at the izakaya Daichi, a little hungry, not sure what the dishes are. You do not drink alcohol tonight. Order drinks and food, ask about a dish you do not know, then ask for the bill.
topics.openerEn: Greet the customer loudly and cheerfully as the izakaya owner, hand over the hot towel and ask about drinks first.
ideasEn: Order a soft drink
Ask what a dish on the wall is
Order two or three dishes with numbers
Ask for the bill
startersJa: ウーロン茶を 一つ おねがいします。
これは 何ですか。
やきとりを 二つ ください。

topics.titleJa: デパートで プレゼントを 買う
topics.titleEn: Buying a present at the department store
topics.situationEn: You are a customer looking for a present (for your teacher, your mother or a friend's birthday) with a budget of about 3,000 yen. Explain who it is for, compare two items, decide, and ask for gift wrapping.
topics.openerEn: Greet the customer in very polite shop language and ask what they are looking for.
ideasEn: Say who the present is for
Ask the price and say your budget
Ask to see another colour or a cheaper one
Decide and ask for wrapping
startersJa: 母の たんじょうびの プレゼントです。
この ネクタイは いくらですか。
これを ください。

topics.titleJa: サイズを かえて もらう
topics.titleEn: Exchanging something that does not fit
topics.situationEn: Yesterday you bought a shirt here but it is too small. You have the receipt. Explain the problem and ask to exchange it for a bigger size; if that size is sold out, decide between another colour, waiting a week, or a refund.
topics.openerEn: Greet the customer politely and ask how you can help; when you hear the problem, check the receipt and the stock (you decide what is in stock).
ideasEn: Say when you bought it and what is wrong
Ask for a bigger size
React if it is sold out and choose another option
Thank her
startersJa: きのう この シャツを 買いましたが、小さいです。
もっと 大きいのは ありますか。
とりかえて もらえますか。

topics.titleJa: 駅で 行き方を 聞く
topics.titleEn: Asking the way at the station
topics.situationEn: You are at the station and want to go to the art museum (or another place in town) but do not know which train or exit to take. Ask the station staff which platform, how long it takes and how much the ticket is.
topics.openerEn: As station staff, notice the learner looking at the route map and ask briskly whether you can help.
ideasEn: Say where you want to go
Ask which platform and which train
Ask how long it takes and the fare
Repeat the directions to check, then thank him
startersJa: すみません、美術館は どの 電車ですか。
何番線ですか。
いくらですか。

topics.situationEn: You left your bag (or umbrella) on the train you just got off. Tell the station staff what it looks like, what is inside, and which train and car you were on.
topics.openerEn: As station staff, see that the learner looks worried and ask what happened; then ask the questions needed to find the item (colour, size, contents, which train).
ideasEn: Say what you lost and where
Describe the colour, size and what is inside
Say which train you took and where you sat
Give your name and phone number
startersJa: 電車に かばんを 忘れました。
黒くて 小さい かばんです。
中に さいふと ノートが あります。

topics.situationEn: You do not feel well (choose: a cold with a sore throat, a stomach ache, or a headache since last night). You are in the consultation room. Explain your symptoms and since when, answer the doctor's questions, and make sure you understand the advice about medicine and rest.
topics.openerEn: As the doctor, greet the patient gently and ask what is wrong today; speak slowly and check that they understand.
ideasEn: Say where it hurts
Say since when and whether you have a fever
Ask whether you may go to school or take a bath
Ask how many times a day to take the medicine
startersJa: きのうから 頭が 痛いです。
熱が あります。
薬は 一日に 何回 飲みますか。

topics.titleJa: コンビニで 買い物
topics.situationEn: You are a customer buying lunch. You cannot find something (batteries, or the onigiri), so ask where it is. At the register answer the usual questions: warm the bento? a bag? chopsticks?
topics.openerEn: As the konbini clerk, greet the customer brightly; help them find things, then ask the usual register questions.
ideasEn: Ask where something is
Ask whether they have a certain item
Answer about warming up the bento and the bag
Pay
startersJa: すみません、電池は どこですか。
はい、おねがいします。
ふくろは いりません。

topics.titleJa: コンビニで 荷物を 送る
topics.titleEn: Sending a parcel at the convenience store
topics.situationEn: You want to send a box of presents to a friend in Osaka from the convenience store. Ask how to do it, what to write on the slip, how much it costs and when it arrives. On hard: you also need to receive a parcel that arrived for you.
topics.openerEn: As the konbini clerk, greet the customer and, seeing the box, ask whether they want to send it; explain the delivery slip in simple steps.
ideasEn: Say you want to send a parcel and where to
Ask what to write on the slip
Ask how much it is and when it arrives
Say what is inside
startersJa: この 荷物を 大阪へ 送りたいです。
ここに 何を 書きますか。
いつ 着きますか。

topics.situationEn: You are visiting the art museum. Buy a ticket (ask about a student discount), ask the closing time, whether photos are allowed and where the lockers are.
topics.openerEn: As the museum receptionist, welcome the visitor crisply and politely and ask how many tickets they need.
ideasEn: Buy a ticket and ask the price
Ask what time the museum closes
Ask whether you may take photos
Ask where the lockers or the café are
startersJa: 学生 一枚 おねがいします。
何時までですか。
写真は いいですか。

topics.situationEn: You are a visitor (a student intern on your first day) arriving at Midori Design. You have an appointment with Murakami-san at 10:00. Say who you are and whom you came to see, and follow the small talk while you wait.
topics.openerEn: You happen to be at the entrance when the visitor arrives: greet them, ask who they are and whom they have come to see, then make small talk while they wait.
ideasEn: Say your name and school
Say you have an appointment and with whom
Answer the small talk (was it easy to find?)
Ask where to wait or where the toilet is
startersJa: おはよう ございます。〜と 申します。
10時に 村上さんと 約束が あります。
こちらで 待っても いいですか。

wordsJa.ja: お世話に なります
wordsJa.kana: おせわに なります

topics.titleJa: 銀行の ことを 聞く
topics.titleEn: Asking a banker about opening an account
topics.situationEn: You need a Japanese bank account for your part-time pay. Your neighbour Shun works at a bank, so you ask him what you need to bring, how long it takes and how to use the ATM.
topics.openerEn: Ask how the learner is settling in; when they bring up the bank, explain calmly as a bank employee what is needed (you decide the details: residence card, seal or signature, address).
ideasEn: Say why you need an account
Ask what to bring
Ask how long it takes and whether it costs money
Ask how to send money to Cambodia
startersJa: 銀行の 口座を 作りたいです。
何が 必要ですか。
どのくらい かかりますか。

topics.titleJa: 先生と 宿題の 話
topics.titleEn: Talking to your teacher about homework
topics.situationEn: After class you talk to your teacher. Choose one: you forgot your homework at home, you did not understand one part, or you will be absent next week and want the homework early. Explain honestly and agree on what to do.
topics.openerEn: As the teacher, notice the learner staying behind after class and ask kindly whether something is the matter.
ideasEn: Apologise and say what happened
Say which page or part you did not understand
Ask until when you can hand it in
Promise what you will do
startersJa: 先生、すみません。宿題を うちに 忘れました。
ここが わかりません。
あした 持って 来ます。

topics.titleEn: Asking your teacher for study advice
topics.situationEn: You want to pass the JLPT (N4 this year, N3 next year) but your listening and kanji are weak and you have little time because of university assignments. Ask your teacher for a study plan.
topics.openerEn: As the teacher, ask how the learner's studies are going; when they ask for advice, first find out how they study now, then give two or three concrete suggestions.
ideasEn: Say your goal and when the exam is
Say what is weak and how you study now
Ask how to practise listening
Repeat the plan to confirm
startersJa: 12月に N4を 受けたいです。
聞き取りが 苦手です。
どうやって 勉強したら いいですか。

topics.titleJa: やさしい 面接の 練習
topics.situationEn: Murakami-san offered to do a relaxed practice interview for an internship at Midori Design. You are the candidate: introduce yourself, say what you study, what you have built, why Japan, and ask one question at the end.
topics.openerEn: As a supportive senior, tell the learner this is only practice, then start with "please introduce yourself" and ask friendly follow-up questions; after a few answers give one short piece of advice.
ideasEn: Introduce yourself in three sentences
Say what you study and what you made
Say why you want to work in Japan
Ask a question about the team
startersJa: 〜と 申します。カンボジアから 来ました。
大学で ITを 勉強して います。
チームで アプリを 作った ことが あります。

wordsJa.ja: よろしく お願いします
wordsJa.kana: よろしく おねがいします

topics.situationEn: You are a candidate for a junior engineer position at Kurogane System. The interviewer keeps asking "why?" and "concretely?". Stay calm, answer with the conclusion first, give one concrete example with a number, and admit honestly what you cannot do yet.
topics.openerEn: As the strict interviewer, start without small talk: ask for a one-minute self-introduction, then press every vague answer with "なぜですか" or "具体的には". Never be rude; acknowledge a good answer with a short nod.
ideasEn: Give a short self-introduction
State your strength with a concrete example
Explain why this company
Answer a weakness question honestly
Ask one question at the end
startersJa: 結論から 申しますと、…
具体的には、3人の チームで …
まだ 経験は ありませんが、…

topics.situationEn: Second part of the interview at Kurogane System: the HR officer checks facts from her sheet (when you can start, your Japanese level, where you will live, overtime, salary expectations) and watches the clock. Answer briefly and exactly, and ask her about training or working hours.
topics.openerEn: As the HR officer, say that you have a few questions to confirm and ten minutes; go through them in a business-like way and note the answers.
ideasEn: Say when you graduate and when you can start
Say your JLPT level and how you keep studying
Answer about overtime and moving to Japan
Ask about training or working hours
startersJa: 来年の 3月に 卒業する 予定です。
4月から 働く ことが できます。
研修は ありますか。

topics.titleJa: ごみの 日を 聞く
topics.titleEn: Asking the neighbour about garbage day
topics.situationEn: You have just moved into the apartment and do not know the rubbish rules. You meet your neighbour in the corridor: ask which days are for which rubbish, where to put it and by what time.
topics.openerEn: Greet your new neighbour warmly in the corridor; when they ask, explain the rubbish days and place (you decide them, e.g. burnable on Monday and Thursday, plastic on Wednesday, by 8 a.m.).
ideasEn: Greet and say you moved in recently
Ask what day the rubbish goes out
Ask where and until what time
Ask about bottles, cans or plastic
startersJa: すみません、ごみの 日は いつですか。
どこに 出しますか。
何時までですか。

topics.situationEn: You want to invite your friend to do something this weekend (a film, soccer in the park, ramen, the museum). Their first date does not work for them, so you have to find another day, then fix the time and meeting place.
topics.openerEn: Chat for a moment as a friend; when invited, be happy but say that the first day suggested is not possible (give a reason), so that the learner has to propose another time.
ideasEn: Ask whether they are free at the weekend
Invite them with 〜ませんか
Suggest another day
Decide the time and place to meet
startersJa: 土曜日は ひまですか。
いっしょに 映画を 見ませんか。
10時に 駅で 会いましょう。

topics.situationEn: The Moris invited you to their home for tea. You brought a small present from Cambodia. Greet them at the door, hand over the present, accept tea and cake politely, compliment the house, and say goodbye when it is time.
topics.openerEn: As the host, welcome the guest at the door, invite them in and offer slippers and tea; show interest in the present.
ideasEn: Say the polite phrases when entering
Give the present and say what it is
Accept or politely refuse a second cup
Compliment something and say thank you when leaving
startersJa: おじゃまします。
これは カンボジアの お茶です。どうぞ。
そろそろ 失礼します。

topics.titleJa: 休みを お願いする
topics.situationEn: You are an intern at Midori Design. You need next Friday off (a university exam, or your sister's wedding at home). Ask your superior politely, explain the reason, and say how your task will be covered.
topics.openerEn: As the superior at your desk, notice the learner waiting to speak and ask what it is; when they ask for the day off, ask about the state of their current task before deciding.
ideasEn: Ask whether they have a moment
Ask for the day off and give the reason
Report how far your task is and who will cover
Thank them
startersJa: 今、少し よろしいですか。
来週の 金曜日に 休みを いただきたいんですが。
仕事は 木曜日までに 終わらせます。

wordsJa.ja: 申し訳 ありません
wordsJa.kana: もうしわけ ありません

topics.titleJa: 先輩に バグの 相談
topics.titleEn: Asking a senior for help with a bug
topics.situationEn: You are an intern on the development team. The login screen of the app you are working on shows an error since this morning and you have been stuck for two hours. Ask a senior for help: say what you wanted to do, what happens, and what you already tried.
topics.openerEn: As a senior engineer, see the learner frowning at the screen and ask how it is going; when they explain, ask what they tried and when it started, and praise asking early.
ideasEn: Ask whether they have time now
Say what happens and since when
Say what you already tried
Confirm what you will do next
startersJa: すみません、今 ちょっと いいですか。
ログインの 画面で エラーが 出ます。
もう 一度 入れて みましたが、だめでした。

topics.titleJa: 写真を お願いする
topics.titleEn: Asking someone to take your photo
topics.situationEn: You want a photo of yourself in a nice spot to send to your family in Cambodia. Ask the person nearby to take it, explain what should be in the picture, thank them, and chat a little about who the photo is for.
topics.openerEn: You are nearby (on your walk or at work); when the learner asks, agree kindly, ask what should be in the photo and afterwards ask who they will send it to.
ideasEn: Politely ask them to take a photo
Say what you want in the picture
Ask for one more
Say who you will send it to
startersJa: すみません、写真を おねがいします。
もう 一枚 おねがいします。
家族に 送ります。

twists.en: It suddenly starts raining outside; the partner notices and comments, maybe asks whether the learner has an umbrella.
The partner's phone buzzes; they glance at it and tell you briefly who it was.
A small dog runs by, chased by its laughing owner; the partner reacts and asks whether the learner likes dogs.
An announcement says the train is about ten minutes late; the partner sighs or explains and comments on it.
Someone nearby (or the partner) spills a little coffee; a quick apology, a napkin, a laugh, then back to the chat.
The partner remembers that today is the birthday of someone they know (a family member or colleague) and asks the learner for a present idea.
The partner gets a short call from work, excuses themselves politely, answers in two sentences and comes back with an apology.
A calm announcement says that this is only a test of the emergency broadcast for next week's earthquake drill; the partner explains what a drill is and asks whether Cambodia has earthquakes.
The neighbourhood cat strolls up and sits down nearby; the partner tells the learner its name.
The wind blows petals or leaves (according to the season) over both of you; the partner comments on the season.
The partner offers the learner a small taste of something new (a sweet, a snack, a piece of cake) and asks how it is.
A song the partner loves starts playing in the background; they say so and ask what music the learner likes.
The partner suddenly asks how to say "thank you" or "hello" in Khmer, tries to repeat it and asks whether the pronunciation is right.
Someone the partner knows from town passes by and waves; the partner waves back and tells the learner in one sentence who it was.
The partner's stomach rumbles; they laugh, admit they skipped a meal and ask what the learner ate today.
The partner suddenly notices how much the learner's Japanese has improved, says so sincerely and asks how they practise.
The partner shows a photo on their phone (their pet, grandchild, a dish they made, a place they visited) and asks whether the learner has a photo of home.
The partner notices a poster for a local event (a concert, an exhibition, the town festival) and asks whether the learner would like to go.
The partner feels thirsty and offers to get drinks from the vending machine; they ask what the learner would like.
Quiet closing-time music starts; the partner explains that the place closes soon but says there are still a few minutes.
The partner playfully gives the learner a one-word quiz: they point at something nearby and ask what it is called in Japanese, then praise or teach the word.
The table next to yours shouts a cheerful "kanpai!"; the partner laughs and explains the custom, then asks what people say in Cambodia.
The partner fans themselves and remarks how warm (or chilly, according to the season) it is today, and asks whether this is normal weather in Cambodia.
A delivery person arrives with a parcel; the partner deals with it in a few seconds and tells the learner what they ordered.
